summary: Owner-run family KG (40 staff, EUR 2-5 M); our EUR 387 k is likely 8-19 % of its turnover. The owner prices from a two-year-old spreadsheet, offered to walk us through his calculation and calls us an important reference customer. Settles below its own ask (asked +0.2 %, gave -1.3 %). Sup:70360 is qualified on the coupling guard and holds 50 % of the motor bracket. Open deep; check current indices against its old spreadsheet, ask for its breakdown.
notes: Wants to keep us as reference customer and its 100 % coupling-guard share; fears volume moving to Strasser (70360). No payment complaint although we pay 9.2 days late on average (76 % of invoices over 5 days late). Green scorecard but 34 complaints in 3 years and two open 8D. Do not cite Strasser's bracket price: it is higher (16.11 vs 15.63).

tactics: Open deep; if current material and energy indices fell, cite them: its spreadsheet is two years old.
Ask it to share the hourly-rate and material breakdown it offered, then argue from its own cost shares.
Point out sup:70360 is qualified on the coupling guard and could take volume.
Offer to keep it as sole source on the coupling guard in exchange for the price step.
Expect 'a fair point' and keep moving in small steps; one argument kind per round.
